record.paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
record.original_question: The source states that every Sobolev space H_0^m(T^1), m≥1, is filled by almost periodic solutions of KdV. Do most of those almost periodic solutions persist under small Hamiltonian perturbations of the equation?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.3.3 (S. Kuksin) Any Sobolev space H{)(Tl), m ~ 1, is filled by almost periodic solutions of (KdV). Do most of them persist under small Hamiltonian perturbations of the equation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Korteweg–de Vries equation
  u_t + u_{xxx} - 6 u u_x = 0,  x ∈ T^1 = R/Z,
under periodic boundary conditions, regarded as an infinite-dimensional integrable Hamiltonian system on the Sobolev spaces H_0^m(T^1) = { u ∈ H^m(T^1) : ∫_{T^1} u dx = 0 }, m ≥ 1. By means of the Birkhoff coordinates (action–angle variables built from the periodic spectrum of the associated Hill operator), every such Sobolev space H_0^m(T^1) is foliated by invariant tori of arbitrary (possibly infinite) dimension; in particular, H_0^m(T^1) is filled by almost periodic solutions of KdV (solutions whose action vector has infinitely many nonzero components, corresponding to invariant tori of infinite dimension).

Question: For a generic small Hamiltonian perturbation
  u_t + u_{xxx} - 6 u u_x + ε ∂_x ∇ K(u) = 0
of the KdV equation (with K a sufficiently smooth Hamiltonian on H_0^m(T^1) and ε sufficiently small), does most of the family of almost periodic solutions of unperturbed KdV — i.e., a subset of the corresponding infinite-dimensional invariant tori of positive measure in an appropriate sense — persist as almost periodic solutions of the perturbed equation?
artifact.status_search_result: Available literature confirms the persistence of finite-gap (quasi-periodic, finite-dimensional torus) solutions of KdV under small Hamiltonian and quasi-linear perturbations, and recent works (e.g. on large KAM tori for quasi-linear perturbations of KdV, and on almost periodic solutions for derivative NLS) extend KAM techniques. However, surveys note that results on almost periodic (infinite-dimensional torus) solutions, especially for KdV-type equations with unbounded perturbations, remain sparse, and no result establishing persistence of "most" almost periodic KdV solutions under general small Hamiltonian perturbations has been found. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Large KAM tori for quasi-linear perturbations of KdV
status_evidence.snippet: Persistence of space periodic multi-solitons (finite-gap solutions) of arbitrary size under quasi-linear Hamiltonian perturbations.
status_evidence.claim: Persistence is established for finite-dimensional (finite-gap) tori, not for almost periodic (infinite-dimensional) tori.

status_evidence.title: On the construction of almost periodic solutions for the derivative NLS
status_evidence.snippet: Investigations into almost periodic solutions, especially in settings involving unbounded perturbations, are remarkably sparse.
status_evidence.claim: Almost periodic KAM results for KdV-type equations with unbounded perturbations remain largely undeveloped.

status_evidence.title: Hamiltonian PDEs (Kuksin, Handbook chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Persistence of finite-gap solutions of KdV under small Hamiltonian perturbations established via KAM; almost periodic case posed as a problem.
status_evidence.claim: Question of persistence of almost periodic KdV solutions stated as an open problem.
